title: Step Functions: state machines and long-running orchestration

videos.script: An order is not one request. It is a check, a wait, a message to the warehouse, and sometimes a person who has to answer. {{order}} Written as one function, that sequence breaks in the middle. The function times out, or fails after half the steps, and nobody knows which half. Step Functions takes the sequence out of your code. You write it down as a state machine, a JSON document, and the service runs it and remembers where it is. {{document}} In this lesson moto really runs one. You will watch two orders take two different paths, and read the history of each. {{paths}} Then the two types. Standard runs for up to a year and happens exactly once. Express lasts five minutes and costs a fraction. You will work out how big that fraction is, and what it buys. {{price}} Then failure. A retry that waits one second, then two, then gives up and hands over to a catch. And why a retry means your task must be safe to run twice. {{retry}} Last, waiting. A timer, a token that a store hands back, and a job the service follows to its end. Nothing of yours runs while the execution waits. {{wait}}
